S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

symptom.disease_info: Persistent Depressive Disorder (PDD), or dysthymia, is characterized by a chronically low mood lasting at least two years in adults, accompanied by other depressive features that are present more days than not. Individuals often describe it as a longstanding sense of gloom or joylessness rather than discrete mood episodes, and they may function outwardly while experiencing significant internal distress and reduced quality of life. The course is typically insidious and protracted, with onset often linked to enduring stressors or personality vulnerabilities rather than a single dramatic event. It is distinguished from major depressive disorder by its chronicity and generally milder but persistent symptoms, though the two can coexist when more severe episodes are superimposed on the chronic low mood.

patient.personality: Larry is a highly creative, achievement‑driven technologist who juggles many artistic and social pursuits while maintaining a meticulous, disciplined approach to work and finances.
patient.stressor: About two and a half years ago, Larry was promoted into a senior product leadership role just as his company began an aggressive restructuring, increasing his workload, responsibility for mentoring younger teams, and pressure to deliver ambitious releases on tight timelines. Initially he responded by throwing himself into work, staying late, cutting back on guitar, painting, and social activities, telling himself it was a temporary sprint that would pay off with stock options and recognition. As months turned into years, the relentless pace, constant context‑switching between strategic planning and hands‑on coding, and a series of under‑resourced launches left him feeling chronically depleted and detached from the creativity that had once energized him, yet he kept pushing to meet expectations and maintain his careful budget and future plans. Over time, he noticed that his nights were increasingly dominated by lying awake cycling through work problems and financial contingencies, and when this persistent pattern began eroding his performance and his enjoyment of even his favorite hobbies, he finally decided to seek psychiatric help at the urging of a colleague who noticed his ongoing struggle.
patient.chief_complaint: “I can’t seem to sleep through the night anymore, and it’s been going on for years now.”

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.
S024.manifestation: For a long time now it’s like there’s this gray film over everything—work, hanging out with friends, even playing guitar—where I can go through the motions and crack jokes in meetings, but underneath I just feel flat and kind of hopeless, like the part of me that used to get genuinely excited about anything has burned out.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: I used to love cooking and trying new restaurants with friends, but over the past couple of years my appetite has really dropped off—most days I just grab something quick at my desk because food feels like fuel I have to choke down rather than something I actually want.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: Most nights I fall asleep okay but then I’m up two or three times, lying there at 3 or 4 a.m. with my brain looping through bug lists, release deadlines, and whether I’m saving enough for retirement, and I just can’t shut it off long enough to get back into any kind of deep sleep.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: Even on weekends when I technically get enough hours in bed, I wake up feeling like I’ve pulled an all-nighter, so just getting through a normal workday or picking up my guitar after dinner feels like I’m dragging a weighted blanket around on my shoulders.
